desc:
You may delete one contiguous block of elements (possibly empty) from the array nums of positive integers so that the sum of the remaining elements is divisible by p. You are not allowed to delete the whole array.

Return the minimum number of elements you must delete, or -1 if it is impossible.

nums = [3, 1, 4, 2], p = 6  -> 1   (delete [4]; the rest sums to 6)
nums = [6, 3, 5, 2], p = 9  -> 2   (delete [5, 2]; the rest sums to 9)
nums = [1, 2, 3],    p = 7  -> -1
hints: Let need = total % p. If it is 0 the answer is 0. Otherwise you must delete a block whose sum leaves remainder need modulo p.
Use prefix sums modulo p. A block ending at prefix j and starting after prefix i has remainder (r_j - r_i) mod p, which should equal need.

For each j, look up the latest earlier prefix with remainder (r_j - need) mod p in a dictionary (storing the last index for every remainder, remainder 0 at index 0). Minimise j - i, and reject the answer n (whole array).
editorial: Removing a block changes the total by the block sum, so the remaining sum is divisible by p exactly when the block sum is congruent to need = total mod p. If need = 0 nothing has to be removed.

Otherwise scan the prefix remainders r_j. A block ending at prefix j must start right after a prefix i with r_i = (r_j - need) mod p; the shortest block uses the latest such i, so store the most recent index per remainder and update it after the lookup. Track the minimum length. If the best block is the whole array (length n) it is not allowed, so report -1. O(n) time and O(min(n, p)) space.
